question.text: Chola Capital LLP is applying to SEBI to act as the Investment Manager of a proposed Cat II AIF. The Chief Investment Officer is reviewing the entity's balance sheet. Which of the following is the MOST CRITICAL 'fit and proper' test the Manager entity must meet under the SEBI intermediaries framework?

answer.text: The Manager must have a minimum paid-up share capital of INR 100 crore.
The Manager must be a listed public company.

Satisfy the 'fit and proper person' criteria specified in Schedule II of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 — covering integrity, reputation and character, no restraint orders or convictions, financial competence based on net worth and solvency, and no wilful-defaulter history.
The Manager must employ at least 25 portfolio managers registered with APMI.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that managers should satisfy the fit-and-proper requirements specified in Schedule II of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008. The registration criteria include integrity, reputation and character, no restraint orders or convictions, financial competence based on net worth and solvency, and no wilful-defaulter history. The Trap: Option A invents an INR 100 crore paid-up capital rule for the Manager entity itself. Option B fabricates a listing requirement. Option D invents an APMI employee head-count rule. Note: The correct anchor is Schedule II of the SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 — qualitative and financial fit-and-proper criteria, not a fixed share-capital minimum.
